items.question: Why are you interested in Cloudflare's Software Engineering Internship? What products or features are you interested in building?
items.problem:
Expected "Most of what I build ends up being about safety boundaries in automated systems, which is why Cloudflare's network layer interests me. When I built a Playwright-based job-application agent in TypeScript, the hard part was not making the browser do things, it was deciding where automation should stop. I used SQLite as the single source of truth because state divergence across processes makes browser automation dangerous, put every mutating capability behind fail-closed flags like SUBMIT_ENABLED that never default on, and architecturally prevented free-text and demographic fields from being auto-filled. I also built a validation ladder from unit-confirmed to live-mutation-confirmed so a capability is never called working just because it passed against a fixture. That is the same instinct behind infrastructure that sits in front of millions of sites: failure modes are the product.

I would want to work on developer-facing edge compute and the tooling around it, or on abuse and anomaly detection. I currently build the ML core of an anomaly-detection system, including temporal sequence modeling over event streams and a learning-to-rank layer, because an alert system that fires too often creates a second problem rather than solving the first."; page shows "Undergrad"
